Serious and fatal crashes in 15068, 2005–2024

PennDOT records, 2005–2024 · Updated Sept. 23, 2026

PennDOT recorded 150 crashes from 2005 through 2024 that killed or seriously injured someone in the three cities: 73 in Lower Burrell, 70 in New Kensington and 7 in Arnold. They killed 38 people and seriously injured 145. From 2020 through 2024 there were 44 such crashes, which killed 7 people. Of the 146 crashes with a mapped location, the most were on Leechburg Road (16), Stevenson Boulevard (12) and Greensburg Road (11), where 6 people died, more than on any other road. Sixteen of the mapped crashes hit a pedestrian; those crashes killed 3 people.

Source: PennDOT crash data

Roads with the most serious crashes

To count crashes by road, each of the 146 crashes with a mapped location is matched to the nearest named road in the map data, if one is within 100 feet (30 m). These road counts use only the mapped crashes; the totals above come from PennDOT's yearly counts, which also include 4 crashes with no recorded location.

What kind of crashes

The most common were angle crashes (45), crashes into a fixed object (39), crashes that hit a pedestrian (16), rear-end crashes (15) and head-on crashes (14). The other 17 were non-collision crashes, opposite-direction sideswipes, other crashes and same-direction sideswipes. Angle crashes killed the most people, 15. For their number, head-on crashes were the deadliest: 5 people died in 14 of them. Sixteen of the mapped crashes hit a pedestrian; those crashes killed 3 people.

The last five years

From 2020 through 2024 there were 44 such crashes, which killed 7 people: 24 in New Kensington, 20 in Lower Burrell and 0 in Arnold. In the five years before, 2015 through 2019, there were 35, which killed 6.

Source: PennDOT crash data

What this data does and doesn't include

PennDOT fatal and suspected-serious-injury crashes (police-reported), 2005-2024, from the bencarneiro/ntsb mirror of PennDOT crash data; spot-checked against PennDOT's full statewide CRASH files for 2012-2016.

Only crashes that killed someone or left someone with a suspected serious injury are here; crashes with minor injuries or damage only are not. Each crash is counted in the city where PennDOT's records place it. 4 of the 150 crashes have no recorded location, so they are in the totals but not on the map or in the road and collision counts.

Source: PennDOT crash data
